reviews.author: r96sk
reviews.content: A solid enough send off for this 'Venom' trilogy. 'Venom: The Last Dance' is decently amusing and produces enough entertainment with its plot. I didn't personally find it overly funny, though the person a few seats across from me had an absolute blast - never a bad thing seeing people enjoy themselves! Tom Hardy remains the key element of these films, they would be far less enjoyable without his presence. There's a nice montage of sorts towards the end, it admittedly didn't 'hit' all that much for me but I imagine it's effective for proper fans of the series. Rhys Ifans and Chiwetel Ejiofor stick out most from the other characters.

reviews.author: Mangoturtle
reviews.content:
The other two at the very least were enjoyable. This one, not so much.

The villian is forced, the movie feels so chopped up, there's no threat because the creatures and Eddie both just heal each other. It had bad dialogue for some scenes, and a weird sub plot about shoes.

Oh, and also, one of Eddie's flashbacks he wasn't even there for.

reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: Perhaps this was just one sequel too many as the story here is really rather thin, but there's still enough chemistry between "Eddie" (Tom Hardy) and his eponymous symbion to raise a smile or two. This time it's not just the pursuing human population that's a problem for them, but there are creatures from the homeworld of "Venom" homing in on their unique "codex" so that they can help free their leader from incarceration to wreak havoc on the universe. Along the way, they encounter the hippie "Martin" (Rhys Ifans) and his family and cadge a lift in their VW camper-van whilst offering a fairly tuneless rendition of some David Bowie. It all builds up to a fairly predictable denouement with humanity facing some tough choices, the seemingly indestructible aliens on the verge of success and our intrepid partnership having to consider the ultimate sacrifice. Yep, we've seen it all before and though the visual effects are pretty impressive, that's not really enough to sustain it as it rather procedurally rolls along. There is occasionally some wit in the script and Hardy looks like he's having fun, but Chiwetel Ejiofor is largely under-used and it relies far too heavily on repetitive combat scenes to really make it stand out amidst the surfeit of 2024 comic-book derivatives. It's all watchable enough, but it's not a patch on the first one from 2018.

reviews.author: TurkBinge
reviews.content: Venom: The Last Dance expands on the chaotic relationship between Eddie Brock and his symbiote Venom with more depth, tension, and humor, while also introducing a menacing new adversary in the form of the Xenophages. But yet, this cartonish way ended while making its last dance, really it was kind of last DANCE even writer pen director direction couldn't go with it and make its end like Bollywood was pretty mid honestly ____ we didn’t see venom much for a movie that ends a highly loved trilogy. also I didn’t see the “MAIN BIG BAD GUY of DARKNESS ANNIHILATION EVERYTHING” do anything. THAT GUY and CODEX concept couldn't go through to see but no MORE BLACK symbiote...

reviews.author: Chandler Danier
reviews.content:
I like all the Venom movies. The humour works. Fun to watch Hardy play a puppet.

Would have been a 10 without that blast door thing. Still a blast. No deductions for runtime.

reviews.author: MovieGuys
reviews.content:
I'm typically not a fan of the Marvel universe films. I find them over stated, not especially intelligent and oftentimes, quite repetitive. 

"Venom" is the rare exception to this rule. For starters there's Tom Hardy, who is, by any measure, an excellent actor. Secondly, there's the interplay between Hardy and Venom which can be genuinely funny. 

This latest and possibly last film in the series, "Venom: The Last Dance", is, I believe, the weakest in the line up. Unlike its predecessors, it feels a little bit rushed and somehow, anti climatic. That said, it still has its moments of engaging humour and not half decent action.

In summary, its a shame to see "Venom" shelved (if in fact that's the case) as its one of the better Marvel universe franchises, with great chemistry between Hardy and his other worldly alter ego, Venom. Worth a look if you enjoyed the other films.

reviews.author: watchnrant
reviews.content:
Okay, here’s the deal with _Venom: The Last Dance_. It’s like ordering your favorite burger and realizing halfway through they forgot the sauce. Tom Hardy? Still killing it as Eddie and Venom—his back-and-forth with himself is weirdly entertaining and even a little emotional. There are some genuinely fun and heartfelt moments that remind you why this duo worked in the first place.

But man, the rest? A hot mess. The plot is all over the map, the new characters are forgettable, and the villain? Weak sauce. It feels like the filmmakers just kind of shrugged and said, “Eh, good enough.” Sure, there are flashes of that buddy-comedy charm, but not enough to save the movie from feeling like it’s limping to the finish line.

If this is the final Venom movie (and I hope it is), I’m not gonna cry about it. It’s a mixed bag—fun in bits, but overall, it’s like Venom himself: a bit too sloppy to fully love.

reviews.author: Dr Nostromo
reviews.content:
64/100

Venom carries a codex, with the potential to destroy the universe, and is being hunted by really big, gnarly, aliens. I was really digging this film - the banter between Eddie and Venom was great, exciting action sets, interesting characters and a pretty good story - until after the river scene. Then the film stalled big time. The protracted VW trip was cringingly awkward and the dance bit in Vegas was silly and weird. The climax, although providing us with a whole bucket full of eye candy and exciting alien combat, didn't really wow me as much as expected. *sigh* -- DrNostromo.com

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: On the run as fugitives, Eddie Brock and Venom are hunted by human military forces and monstrous alien Xenophages, culminating in a heartbreaking final stand to save humanity.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Following their recent battles, Eddie Brock and Venom find themselves on the run from both human military operatives and deadly alien Xenophages sent by Knull, the ancient creator of the symbiotes. As the creatures hunt for the power contained within Venom that could free Knull from his prison, Eddie and his symbiote partner travel across the country toward New York City. The pair are eventually forced into an all-out clash alongside military personnel and newly bonded symbiotes at Area 51 to stop the invading horde. Ultimately, Venom makes a devastating sacrifice to destroy the cosmic threat, saving Eddie's life and preventing universal catastrophe.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: After returning to their universe, fugitive journalist Eddie Brock and his alien partner, Venom, set out for New York City in hopes of clearing Eddie's name. However, their journey is disrupted when they are pursued by General Rex Strickland's military task force, which captures and studies symbiotes at Area 51. At the same time, Knull—the imprisoned dark god of the symbiotes—dispatches monstrous Xenophages to Earth to retrieve a vital energy key called the Codex, which exists because Venom previously resurrected Eddie. While attempting to escape both military forces and relentless alien hunters across Nevada and Las Vegas, Eddie and Venom form unexpected bonds with traveling enthusiasts and old friends. Eventually, the duo is captured and brought to Area 51, where researcher Dr. Teddy Paine attempts to understand the symbiotes' origin. When a massive horde of Xenophages invades the facility, the remaining captured symbiotes break free and bond with human hosts to wage a desperate defense. Realizing that the cosmic key can only be destroyed if one of them perishes, Venom chooses to sacrifice himself to protect Eddie and the world. Venom merges with the attacking Xenophages and drags them into containment acid tanks, destroying the threat as the facility collapses. In the aftermath, Eddie awakens with his criminal record fully expunged, later traveling to New York City to look upon the Statue of Liberty while honoring the memory of his fallen friend.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: In the final chapter of the trilogy, fugitive investigative journalist Eddie Brock and his bonded alien symbiote, Venom, find themselves relentlessly hunted on two fronts. While on the run from a clandestine military organization seeking to capture extraterrestrial symbiotes, they discover they are also targeted by horrific alien predators known as Xenophages. Sent by Knull—the ancient and malevolent god of the symbiote race—these monsters track a unique energy signature bound exclusively to Eddie and Venom. Forced onto a desperate cross-country journey, the codependent duo must navigate military ambushes, unexpected road-trip encounters, and an impending planetary invasion. As their pursuers close in from all sides, Eddie and Venom are forced into a devastating decision that tests the limits of their bond and determines the fate of Earth.
